findings.text: §5's section/todo coverage refusal and §6's terminal-status guard are new write-path refusals placed in `_store.py` without naming the owners to extend: `apply_ops` (the single post-op validation point, which already refuses a terminal `set` at lines 3366–3373 through `_require_transition_verdict`), `validate_landing_patch` (the write-keyed terminal-status/evidence guard at 3248), and `_require_new_section_contracts` (the newly-added-heading structure guard at 1662); a plan that adds two more checks beside these three grows a third refusal path in a module that already holds two.

findings.reason: one predicate owned once (near `derive_impl_from_sections`) and consumed by both the write guard and the roadmap prevents the writer and the readiness surface from disagreeing about what "done" means.
findings.text: §6 (refuse terminal while any declaration is `implementable` or `deferred`) and §9 (whole-plan dependency "satisfied … when none of its sections is left `implementable`") both compute the same "every declaration is `done`" predicate over the same `section_declarations` map, and neither section names a shared owner; the vocabulary and a per-section partial reader already live beside this machinery (`reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py:164` `_reviewed_sections_done`, and the `done`/`implementable`/`deferred` triple inlined at `reckon/_plan_html.py:798`).

findings.reason: as written the SPA cannot see the field §3 adds, so §4's done-when is unreachable unless the plan names a single shared derivation point (or extends `parse_plan`/`serve.py`); otherwise the SPA must re-derive `todos` in JSX, against the binding "the SPA renders; it does not derive".
findings.text: §3 derives `todos` in the typed read (`mcp_views._summary`/`_detail`), but §4 renders it in the SPA, whose plan state is fetched from `serve.py`'s `/plan/<project>/<slug>` endpoint; that endpoint returns `_plan_html.parse_plan(pf)`, not the typed view (it already re-shapes `sections` through `with_section_attempts` at `reckon/serve.py:3055`), and `_summary` is not even handed the `html_text` that the heading text and `#<id>` link require.

findings.reason: the section should either carry these fields on `sections` or state why a parallel list is needed, so the two surfaces cannot drift apart.
findings.text: the `todos` list re-projects the reader's existing `sections` records over the same `section_declarations` (the id and the declaration are already present, and `sections` already carries status), adding only heading text, an in-page link and one `c-close-` comment lookup; the plan does not justify a second per-section list rather than enriching `sections`.
